label: <DEL> step of long sequences that start with q/w/l and have k/z in positions 1-3
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.16% of delimiter steps). 80% of activation mass is on the <DEL> step (recall_idx 0), almost all at L=8-9; the rest falls on the last 1-3 original tokens of the same sequences, and it essentially never fires in the copy phase or before t=5. Which long sequences it fires on depends on their first few tokens: first token q, w or l (about 6x lift) and k or z at original positions 1-3 (e.g. l k k ..., w z k z ...). The strongest activations combine several of these cues, so magnitude grows with how many of them are present and with L. A predicate requiring >=2 of these cues at the DEL step of L>=8 sequences gets about half the mass at ~10% precision. It looks like a distributed code over early-token content, and no single clean rule captures it. It does not fire at the DEL step of short sequences (L<=6) or during copying.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig2=k (+4.81), orig2=z (+4.25), orig3=k (+3.74), orig0=w (+3.46), orig1=k (+3.40), orig0=q (+3.34). Lower it: phase=2 (-7.04), next_out=- (-3.35), orig6=- (-2.30), orig7=- (-2.11).
